Likely pseudoreplicated. Authors performed this experiment 3x and sampled 12 from each, then analyzed data using t-test (so presumably no blocking in model). Thus it would be correct to use n=3 if using all data or n=12 if using only data from one experiment. But performing two-sample t-test for results they claimed to be significant using n=3 returns non-significant p-values so they must not have used n=3. Unclear if authors used n=12 which would be ok if they only used data from 1 repeat of the experiment but they don't mention dropping any data so that likely did not happen. I imagine they used n=3*12=36. Based on asterisk use they seem to claim significance at the 0.01 level so I think they most likely used n=36.
